summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening left-sided chest pain and shortness of breath over five days, found to have bilateral pulmonary emboli on CT angiography. She was treated with heparin initially, then transitioned to enoxaparin and warfarin. Her oxygen requirement improved, and she was discharged on home oxygen at 2 liters per minute. She developed transient acute kidney injury, likely contrast-induced, which resolved with IV fluids. Her heart failure and hypertension were managed with continued beta-blocker therapy and temporary hold of furosemide during renal impairment. Chronic pain was controlled with acetaminophen-codeine. She was discharged in stable condition with instructions to continue anticoagulation, monitor INR and creatinine, and follow up with her physician.
